title: Rather a dull number
mechanism: 1729 is the smallest positive integer that can be written as a sum of two positive cubes in two different ways. Compute each pair the long way: 1³ = 1 and 12³ = 1728, which sum to 1729; 9³ = 729 and 10³ = 1000, which also sum to 1729. Checking every smaller n by brute force (for each n, for every i ≥ 1 with 2i³ ≤ n, ask whether n − i³ is itself a cube) turns up no other case with two distinct unordered pairs — so 1729 really is the first. Ramanujan spotted this on the spot; the check_script re-runs the search to prove it.
